metadata.title: Generative Adversarial Nets
metadata.authors: Ian J. Goodfellow, Jean Pouget-Abadie, Mehdi Mirza, Bing Xu, David Warde-Farley, Sherjil Ozair, Aaron Courville, Yoshua Bengio

nodes.name: Generator $G$
nodes.statement: A differentiable function $G(\bm{z}; \theta_g)$ represented by a multilayer perceptron with parameters $\theta_g$, mapping noise variables $\bm{z} \sim p_{\bm{z}}(\bm{z})$ to data space, implicitly defining the generator distribution $p_g$ over $\bm{x}$.
nodes.statement_clean: A neural network mapping random noise to data space, defining the implicit generative distribution $p_g$.

nodes.name: Discriminator $D$
nodes.statement: A multilayer perceptron $D(\bm{x}; \theta_d)$ outputting a scalar in $[0,1]$ representing the probability that $\bm{x}$ came from the data distribution $p_\text{data}$ rather than from the generator distribution $p_g$.
nodes.statement_clean: A neural network classifier estimating the probability that an input $\bm{x}$ comes from the data rather than from the generator.

nodes.name: Value function $V(D,G)$ of the adversarial game
nodes.statement: $V(D,G) = \mathbb{E}_{\bm{x} \sim p_\text{data}}[\log D(\bm{x})] + \mathbb{E}_{\bm{z} \sim p_{\bm{z}}}[\log(1 - D(G(\bm{z})))]$, used as the payoff in the two-player minimax game between $G$ and $D$.
nodes.statement_clean: Expected log-likelihood that $D$ correctly classifies real and generated samples, used as the minimax objective.

nodes.name: Virtual training criterion $C(G)$
nodes.statement: $C(G) = \max_D V(G,D) = \mathbb{E}_{\bm{x} \sim p_\text{data}}[\log D^*_G(\bm{x})] + \mathbb{E}_{\bm{x} \sim p_g}[\log(1 - D^*_G(\bm{x}))]$.
nodes.statement_clean: The maximum of the value function over $D$, viewed as a function of the generator alone.

nodes.name: Kullback--Leibler divergence
nodes.statement: For distributions $p, q$, $KL(p \| q) = \int p(\bm{x}) \log \frac{p(\bm{x})}{q(\bm{x})} d\bm{x}$, a non-negative measure of dissimilarity that is zero iff $p = q$.
nodes.origin_citation: Kullback & Leibler 1951; Cover & Thomas, Elements of Information Theory

nodes.name: Jensen--Shannon divergence
nodes.statement: For distributions $p, q$, $JSD(p \| q) = \tfrac{1}{2} KL\!\left(p \,\big\|\, \tfrac{p+q}{2}\right) + \tfrac{1}{2} KL\!\left(q \,\big\|\, \tfrac{p+q}{2}\right)$, symmetric, bounded, non-negative, and zero iff $p=q$.

nodes.name: Adversarial minimax game for generative modeling
nodes.statement: Solve the two-player minimax problem $\min_G \max_D V(D,G) = \mathbb{E}_{\bm{x} \sim p_\text{data}}[\log D(\bm{x})] + \mathbb{E}_{\bm{z} \sim p_{\bm{z}}}[\log(1 - D(G(\bm{z})))]$ with respect to the generator distribution $p_g$ induced by $G$.
nodes.statement_clean: Find a generator $G$ minimizing the worst-case log-likelihood that $D$ correctly classifies real vs.\ generated samples.

nodes.name: Minimax game definition
nodes.statement: $\min_G \max_D V(D, G) = \mathbb{E}_{\bm{x} \sim p_\text{data}(\bm{x})}[\log D(\bm{x})] + \mathbb{E}_{\bm{z} \sim p_{\bm{z}}(\bm{z})}[\log(1 - D(G(\bm{z})))]$.

nodes.name: Optimal discriminator closed form
nodes.statement: $D^*_G(\bm{x}) = \dfrac{p_\text{data}(\bm{x})}{p_\text{data}(\bm{x}) + p_g(\bm{x})}$.

nodes.name: Reformulation of $C(G)$ as KL divergences
nodes.statement: $C(G) = -\log 4 + KL\!\left(p_\text{data} \,\big\|\, \tfrac{p_\text{data}+p_g}{2}\right) + KL\!\left(p_g \,\big\|\, \tfrac{p_\text{data}+p_g}{2}\right)$.

nodes.name: Reformulation of $C(G)$ as Jensen--Shannon divergence
nodes.statement: $C(G) = -\log 4 + 2 \cdot JSD(p_\text{data} \| p_g)$.

nodes.name: Optimal discriminator for fixed $G$
nodes.statement: For $G$ fixed, the optimal discriminator is $D^*_G(\bm{x}) = \dfrac{p_\text{data}(\bm{x})}{p_\text{data}(\bm{x}) + p_g(\bm{x})}$.
assumptions: $p_\text{data}$ and $p_g$ are well-defined densities on the same space

nodes.name: Global optimality of $p_g = p_\text{data}$
nodes.statement: The global minimum of the virtual training criterion $C(G)$ is achieved if and only if $p_g = p_\text{data}$, and at that point $C(G) = -\log 4$.
assumptions: Non-parametric setting: $p_g$ ranges over all densities
$D$ is allowed to attain the optimum $D^*_G$ for each $G$
conclusions: The minimum is attained iff $p_g = p_\text{data}$

nodes.name: Convergence of the adversarial training procedure
nodes.statement: If $G$ and $D$ have enough capacity and at each step the discriminator reaches its optimum given $G$, and $p_g$ is updated to improve $\mathbb{E}_{\bm{x} \sim p_\text{data}}[\log D^*_G(\bm{x})] + \mathbb{E}_{\bm{x} \sim p_g}[\log(1 - D^*_G(\bm{x}))]$, then $p_g$ converges to $p_\text{data}$.
assumptions: $D$ attains its optimum given $G$ at each step
$p_g$ is updated to improve the criterion with sufficiently small steps

nodes.name: Proof of optimal discriminator (Proposition 1)
nodes.statement: Pointwise maximization of the integrand $a \log y + b \log(1-y)$ over $y \in [0,1]$ yields $y = a/(a+b)$, applied with $a = p_\text{data}(\bm{x})$, $b = p_g(\bm{x})$.

nodes.name: Proof of global optimality (Theorem 1)
nodes.statement: Substitute $D^*_G$ into $C(G)$, rewrite the resulting expression as $-\log 4 + 2 \cdot JSD(p_\text{data} \| p_g)$, and use non-negativity of $JSD$ with equality iff distributions match.

nodes.name: Proof of convergence of adversarial training (Proposition 2)
nodes.statement: Treat $V(G,D) = U(p_g, D)$ as a function of $p_g$; the supremum over $D$ is convex in $p_g$, with unique minimum from Theorem 1, so subgradient updates of $p_g$ at the optimal $D$ converge to $p_\text{data}$.

nodes.name: Express $V(G,D)$ as a single integral over $\bm{x}$
nodes.statement: Rewrite $V(G,D) = \int_{\bm{x}} p_\text{data}(\bm{x}) \log D(\bm{x}) + p_g(\bm{x}) \log(1 - D(\bm{x})) d\bm{x}$ by changing variables $\bm{z} \to \bm{x}$ in the second term.

nodes.name: Pointwise optimization of $a\log y + b\log(1-y)$
nodes.statement: For $(a,b) \in \mathbb{R}^2 \setminus \{(0,0)\}$, the function $y \mapsto a \log y + b \log(1-y)$ attains its maximum on $[0,1]$ at $y = \dfrac{a}{a+b}$.

nodes.name: Apply with $a=p_\text{data}, b=p_g$ and conclude
nodes.statement: Setting $a = p_\text{data}(\bm{x})$ and $b = p_g(\bm{x})$ gives $D^*_G(\bm{x}) = \dfrac{p_\text{data}(\bm{x})}{p_\text{data}(\bm{x}) + p_g(\bm{x})}$; $D$ need not be defined outside $\mathrm{Supp}(p_\text{data}) \cup \mathrm{Supp}(p_g)$.

nodes.name: Evaluate $C(G)$ at $p_g = p_\text{data}$
nodes.statement: When $p_g = p_\text{data}$, $D^*_G(\bm{x}) = \tfrac{1}{2}$ and $C(G) = \log\tfrac{1}{2} + \log\tfrac{1}{2} = -\log 4$.

nodes.name: Subtract $-\log 4$ to expose KL divergences
nodes.statement: Subtract $\mathbb{E}_{p_\text{data}}[-\log 2] + \mathbb{E}_{p_g}[-\log 2] = -\log 4$ from $C(G)$ to obtain $C(G) = -\log 4 + KL\!\left(p_\text{data} \,\big\|\, \tfrac{p_\text{data}+p_g}{2}\right) + KL\!\left(p_g \,\big\|\, \tfrac{p_\text{data}+p_g}{2}\right)$.

nodes.name: Recognize Jensen--Shannon divergence
nodes.statement: Identify the previous expression as $C(G) = -\log 4 + 2 \cdot JSD(p_\text{data} \| p_g)$.

nodes.name: Conclude using non-negativity of $JSD$
nodes.statement: Since $JSD(p_\text{data} \| p_g) \geq 0$ with equality iff $p_\text{data} = p_g$, the global minimum $-\log 4$ of $C(G)$ is attained exactly when $p_g = p_\text{data}$.

nodes.name: View $V(G,D)$ as $U(p_g, D)$, convex in $p_g$
nodes.statement: Define $U(p_g, D) := V(G,D)$ as a function of $p_g$; $U$ is convex in $p_g$ for every fixed $D$.

nodes.name: Subgradient inclusion for supremum of convex functions
nodes.statement: For $f(x) = \sup_{\alpha \in \mathcal{A}} f_\alpha(x)$ with each $f_\alpha$ convex in $x$, $\partial f_\beta(x) \subset \partial f(x)$ when $\beta = \arg\sup_\alpha f_\alpha(x)$, so a subgradient at the optimal $D$ is a valid update direction.

nodes.name: Conclude convergence using uniqueness from Theorem 1
nodes.statement: $\sup_D U(p_g, D)$ is convex in $p_g$ with unique global optimum at $p_g = p_\text{data}$ (Thm.~\ref{thm:global-optimality}); sufficiently small subgradient updates of $p_g$ therefore converge to $p_\text{data}$.

nodes.name: Minibatch SGD training of generative adversarial nets
nodes.statement: Iterative minibatch SGD that alternates $k$ ascent steps on $\theta_d$ with one descent step on $\theta_g$ to optimize the minimax game $\min_G \max_D V(D,G)$.
nodes.pseudocode: for number of training iterations: for k steps: sample $\{\bm{z}^{(i)}\}_{i=1}^m \sim p_g$; sample $\{\bm{x}^{(i)}\}_{i=1}^m \sim p_\text{data}$; ascend $\nabla_{\theta_d} \tfrac{1}{m} \sum_i [\log D(\bm{x}^{(i)}) + \log(1 - D(G(\bm{z}^{(i)})))]$; end for; sample $\{\bm{z}^{(i)}\}_{i=1}^m \sim p_g$; descend $\nabla_{\theta_g} \tfrac{1}{m} \sum_i \log(1 - D(G(\bm{z}^{(i)})))$; end for.

nodes.name: Outer training loop
nodes.statement: Repeat the inner discriminator/generator updates for the prescribed number of training iterations.

nodes.name: Inner discriminator loop ($k$ steps)
nodes.statement: Repeat the discriminator update $k$ times per outer iteration.

nodes.name: Sample noise and data minibatches
nodes.statement: Sample minibatch $\{\bm{z}^{(1)}, \dots, \bm{z}^{(m)}\}$ from noise prior $p_g(\bm{z})$ and minibatch $\{\bm{x}^{(1)}, \dots, \bm{x}^{(m)}\}$ from $p_\text{data}(\bm{x})$.

nodes.name: Discriminator gradient ascent
nodes.statement: Update $\theta_d$ by ascending $\nabla_{\theta_d} \tfrac{1}{m} \sum_{i=1}^m \left[ \log D(\bm{x}^{(i)}) + \log(1 - D(G(\bm{z}^{(i)}))) \right]$.

nodes.name: Sample fresh noise minibatch for $G$ update
nodes.statement: After the $k$ discriminator steps, sample a fresh minibatch $\{\bm{z}^{(1)}, \dots, \bm{z}^{(m)}\}$ from the noise prior $p_g(\bm{z})$.

nodes.name: Generator gradient descent
nodes.statement: Update $\theta_g$ by descending $\nabla_{\theta_g} \tfrac{1}{m} \sum_{i=1}^m \log(1 - D(G(\bm{z}^{(i)})))$.

nodes.name: Non-saturating generator objective
nodes.statement: Early in training $\log(1 - D(G(\bm{z})))$ saturates because $D$ confidently rejects $G$'s samples; instead training $G$ to maximize $\log D(G(\bm{z}))$ yields the same fixed point but much stronger early gradients.

nodes.name: Bayes-rule interpretation of $D$'s objective
nodes.statement: The training objective for $D$ can be interpreted as maximizing the log-likelihood for estimating the conditional probability $P(Y=y \mid \bm{x})$, where $Y=1$ if $\bm{x} \sim p_\text{data}$ and $Y=0$ if $\bm{x} \sim p_g$.

nodes.name: Practical caveat: parameter-space optimization
nodes.statement: In practice we optimize $\theta_g$ rather than $p_g$ directly; multilayer perceptrons introduce multiple critical points in parameter space, but their empirical performance suggests they are reasonable models despite the lack of theoretical guarantees.

nodes.name: Helvetica scenario / mode collapse
nodes.statement: If $G$ is trained too much without updating $D$, $G$ may collapse too many values of $\bm{z}$ to the same value of $\bm{x}$, losing diversity needed to model $p_\text{data}$ -- the so-called ``Helvetica scenario''.

nodes.name: MNIST and TFD Parzen-window log-likelihood evaluation
nodes.statement: Adversarial nets trained on MNIST and Toronto Face Database; test-set log-likelihood estimated via Gaussian Parzen window fit to generated samples ($\sigma$ chosen by cross-validation). Reported scores: MNIST $225 \pm 2$, TFD $2057 \pm 26$, competitive with DBN, Stacked CAE, and Deep GSN baselines.

nodes.name: CIFAR-10 sample generation
nodes.statement: Adversarial nets trained on CIFAR-10 with both fully-connected and convolutional discriminator / ``deconvolutional'' generator architectures; samples shown in Fig.~\ref{fig:visuals1}(c,d).

nodes.name: Latent-space interpolation
nodes.statement: Digits obtained by linearly interpolating between coordinates in $\bm{z}$ space of the full MNIST model (Fig.~\ref{fig:visuals3}), illustrating smooth transitions in the learned latent representation.
